name: Yeah Yeah Yeahs
label: Touch and Go
lede: Karen O, Nick Zinner and a drummer recruited the day before their first show put out a five-song EP on their own label, let Touch and Go take it national, then turned down the majors, paid for their own debut and spent twenty-five years refusing to make the same record twice.

eras.title: Unitard gets loud
eras.text: Karen Orzolek left Oberlin for NYU, met Nick Zinner at a Lower East Side bar and started an acoustic duo. By the end of 2000 they had a new name, a trashier sound lifted from the Ohio scene she'd seen up close, and a conservatory drummer.

years.src: Stereogum: The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP Turns 20 · Wikipedia: Yeah Yeah Yeahs
years.h: Karen O and Nick Zinner start an acoustic duo called Unitard
years.p: Karen Orzolek, an Oberlin transfer at NYU, meets guitarist [[Nick Zinner|20dc35ec-6cc1-4c66-98a3-4a6116cb3869]] at the Mars Bar. Later that year the duo becomes Yeah Yeah Yeahs and goes "trashy, punky, [and] grimy," in Wikipedia's quoting.
years.xp: The name comes from a New York expression. Karen O had spent time at Oberlin College in Ohio, and Wikipedia credits the new sound to what she saw in the Ohio music scene.

years.cap: Karen O at Brownies, New York
years.src: Wikipedia: Yeah Yeah Yeahs · Stereogum: The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP Turns 20
years.h: Brian Chase joins the day before the first show, opening for the White Stripes
years.p: Invited to open for [[The White Stripes|11ae9fbb-f3d7-4a47-936f-4c0a04d3b3b5]] at the Mercury Lounge, Karen O won't use a drum machine live. [[Brian Chase|a1439b8d-672a-446f-a7ff-6f09d68254b3]], a conservatory-trained friend from Oberlin, joins a day before the show and stays.

years.src: Wikipedia: Yeah Yeah Yeahs · Stereogum: The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP Turns 20
years.h: Five songs, thirteen minutes, on their own Shifty label
years.p: Meant as a demo to get more shows. [[Boss Hog|57648c1f-335d-4216-ba82-508b23b3bcf4]]'s Jerry Teel co-produced it at Funhouse in New York, which doubled as their rehearsal room.
years.xp: Zinner said they put it out because they wanted people to hear it. Nielsen SoundScan later counted more than 71,000 copies sold, and it topped the UK Indie Chart.

eras.title: A pin on SNL and $32 from Wichita
eras.text: One year turned a Lower East Side band into the British press's favorite New Yorkers. Touch and Go put the EP out across the US, Wichita did the same in the UK, and the band walked away from major-label money to make a debut on its own dime.

years.src: Wikipedia: Yeah Yeah Yeahs · Stereogum: The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP Turns 20
years.h: Albert Hammond Jr. wears a Yeah Yeah Yeahs pin on Saturday Night Live
years.p: [[The Strokes|f181961b-20f7-459e-89de-920ef03c7ed0]] guitarist's button gets the band its first big wave of press, followed by a high-profile South by Southwest set.

years.h: Touch and Go reissues the EP in America; Wichita takes the UK
years.p: [[Touch and Go|83a554c5-4fd3-4ec8-9dd5-15989850ea17]] puts the Shifty EP out nationally. In London, Wichita signs them off one song, 'Bang', and pays a first royalty of $32.
years.xp: Wichita's founders flew over and saw them fourth on the bill to Arab on Radar. "Karen O was already a superstar in every way," Mark Bowen told the Guardian. Jo Whiley then played 'Bang' at lunchtime on Radio 1, chorus swearing and all, and it became the label's first top 40 hit.

years.src: Stereogum: The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP Turns 20 · Wikipedia: Yeah Yeah Yeahs
years.h: Coney Island's Siren Festival, then the road with Jon Spencer
years.p: The band plays the Siren Festival in Coney Island and tours with the [[Jon Spencer Blues Explosion|d1ab8ca8-fb9f-4e78-a422-3cd5406dc0b1]]. Rolling Stone's Rob Sheffield writes them up that month.
years.xp: Not everyone bought Karen O's stage act; one critic called it forced. Tom Breihan's answer, writing in Stereogum: "Through the miracle of rock 'n' roll, Karen O had turned herself into a superhero."

years.src: Wikipedia: Fever to Tell · Wikipedia: Yeah Yeah Yeahs
years.h: They skip Reading and pay for their own album
years.p: The band cancels its Reading Festival slot to record, turns down major-label offers to fund the debut, and books the cheap Headgear studio in Brooklyn with [[Dave Sitek|db4bb549-057d-4df7-831e-b4394e2c1359]] of [[TV on the Radio|eb872766-98f6-453d-883f-2ae908a18315]].
years.xp: Why Sitek? They "felt immediately like we were family," and "we didn't know anyone else," the band told Rolling Stone. It was his first of many productions for them.

years.src: Wikipedia: Fever to Tell · Stereogum: The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP Turns 20
years.h: Machine, the second Touch and Go EP
years.p: Three songs from the album sessions, out on [[Touch and Go|83a554c5-4fd3-4ec8-9dd5-15989850ea17]] to tide fans over. Stereogum later called it "relatively slight and forgotten."

eras.title: Real tears in a high school gym
eras.text: Lee Ranaldo talked them into Interscope, where they kept creative control. Fever to Tell sold a million copies worldwide, and 'Maps', a love song Karen O wrote for her boyfriend, carried the album to MTV.

years.src: Wikipedia: Yeah Yeah Yeahs · Wikipedia: Fever to Tell
years.h: Lee Ranaldo talks them into signing with Interscope
years.p: [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]]'s [[Lee Ranaldo|6eb1f3f8-5c5a-41c2-a390-f397a2b824a3]] pushes for the deal, which leaves the band in creative control. Interscope distributes the album they've already paid for.

years.src: Wikipedia: Fever to Tell · Wikipedia: Yeah Yeah Yeahs
years.h: Fever to Tell puts Karen O's sex-and-heartbreak songs on Interscope
years.p: Eleven songs and a hidden track, mixed in London by Zinner and Alan Moulder. Zinner plays the bass parts, uncredited. Cody Critcheloe drew the cover.
years.xp:
Jon Pareles, in Rolling Stone, called Karen O "one excitable girl." Robert Christgau was less charmed by her persona. The New York Times named it the best album of 2003, and it got a Grammy nomination for Best Alternative Music Album.

By March 2009 it had sold more than a million copies worldwide.

years.src: Wikipedia: Maps · Wikipedia: Fever to Tell
years.h: 'Maps': three hours late, real tears
years.p: Karen O wrote 'Maps' about her boyfriend, Liars singer Angus Andrew. He was due at Patrick Daughters's video shoot in a high school gym and turned up three hours late, so the crying on camera is real.
years.xp:
"They were real tears," Karen O said. "I didn't think he was even going to come and this was the song that was written for him." Manager Asif Ahmed said she wrote one hundred percent of the song; one chorus line came from an email she'd sent Andrew.

The video went into heavy MTV rotation in February 2004, the single reached No. 87 on the Hot 100, and it tripled the album's sales.

years.src: Far Out: How an onstage accident changed the life of Karen O · The Guardian: Karen O
years.h: Karen O falls headfirst off the stage in Sydney
years.p: At a warm-up show in Sydney, she climbs over a monitor during 'Rich' and goes over, the 60-pound monitor following her, according to Far Out. Two days later she performs in a wheelchair.
years.xp:
"The next day, I looked like I had elephantitis," she says in Meet Me in the Bathroom, as quoted by Far Out.

She later called the early shows self-destructive: "rolling around on broken glass and getting blind drunk," she told the Guardian. "When I fell headfirst off the stage I realised I had to rethink my whole stage thing."

years.h: Tell Me What Rockers to Swallow: the Fillmore on DVD
years.p: The first DVD collects a concert filmed at the Fillmore in San Francisco, every video so far and interviews.

eras.title: Scrapped, restarted, nearly over
eras.text: The band set out not to make "Fever to Tell part 2" and nearly broke up trying. Show Your Bones came out of scrapped sessions and a fraying friendship between Karen O and Zinner, and still landed at No. 7 in the UK.

years.big: "We just scared the shit out of each other"
q: We just scared the shit out of each other
years.h: The second album gets scrapped and started over
years.p: Back at it with Sitek and Squeak E. Clean, the band junks the first round of Show Your Bones. The Guardian later reported that Karen O and Zinner's relationship got bad enough that she nearly quit.
years.xp: Karen O to NME: "it was a dark and scary realm that we were going into – not that the music was dark and scary it was just totally different." Chase said he didn't understand the record until a month after it was finished.

years.h: Show Your Bones swaps garage noise for acoustic guitars
years.p: The band described it as "what happens when you put your finger in a light socket." It goes to No. 7 in the UK, quadruples Fever to Tell's first-week US sales and earns a second Grammy nomination.
years.xp: Time's Josh Tyrangiel heard the tension in 'Cheated Hearts': "you get the sense that there might be a little tension in this band."

years.h: Imaad Wasif joins the live band, and stays for decades
years.p: The trio has never had a bassist. From 2006 Imaad Wasif fills in on bass, keyboards and guitar on tour, a role he still plays.

years.h: Is Is rescues songs from between the first two albums
years.p: An EP of material written between Fever to Tell and Show Your Bones, produced by Nick Launay. It enters the Billboard 200 at No. 72.
years.xp: The band's announcement: "Summer nights are made for this shit. This shit IS IS made for summer nights."

eras.title: An ARP synth and the top of the Empire State Building
eras.text: With Launay and Sitek they went dance-punk and sold more than ever: It's Blitz! went gold in three countries and 'Heads Will Roll' went double platinum in the UK. Mosquito charted higher still and took a critical beating.

years.h: Zinner brings an ARP synthesizer to the studio on a whim
years.p: For It's Blitz! the band writes everything in the studio, across five of them. Launay said he hadn't seen a band work that way since 1979.

years.h: It's Blitz! leaks, so the band puts it out early
years.p: Slated for April, the album turns up online in February, much to the band's dismay, and the release is pulled forward.

years.h: It's Blitz! goes gold in the US, UK and Australia
years.p: Synths and drum samples instead of garage guitar. It doubles Show Your Bones's US sales and earns a third Grammy nomination.

years.h: 'Heads Will Roll' becomes the band's biggest seller
years.p: The single goes double platinum in the UK and New Zealand, and A-Trak's remix takes it into clubs. Rolling Stone puts it on its list of the 200 greatest dance songs.

years.h: Slint's David Pajo plays bass on the road
years.p: [[David Pajo|85188c46-d3ed-4517-ba78-5d06ec764f1c]] of [[Slint|2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28]] fills the bass spot on tour into 2010.

years.h: Fans pile on the Mosquito cover
years.p: Beomsik Shimbe Shim's artwork for the fourth album draws a wave of complaints. The Guardian's headline said fans think it "sucks."

years.h: Mosquito hits No. 5, the band's highest US chart spot
years.p: [[James Murphy|6b70c46c-5c83-4cc7-99c1-e76b68919c6a]] of [[LCD Soundsystem|2aaf7396-6ab8-40f3-9776-a41c42c8e26b]] joins Sitek and Launay behind the desk. Some critics called it the band's first step backward.
years.xp: Karen O said Mosquito "was the rope ladder thrown down into the ditch for us to climb up and dust ourselves off." The 'Sacrilege' video won two UK Music Video Awards.

years.cap: On the Mosquito tour, Ventura, April 2013
years.h: First band to shoot a video on top of the Empire State Building
years.p: The 'Despair' video is filmed on the skyscraper's roof, a first for any band.

eras.title: On a bit of a hiatus
eras.text: No new album for nine years. Karen O went solo and became a mother, Zinner showed photographs, Chase made drone records, and the band came back in 2017 to play Fever to Tell for a generation that had grown up on it.

years.h: Karen O tells NME the band is "on a bit of a hiatus"
years.p: She cites a lack of inspiration and motivation. Her solo album Crush Songs is already out; Zinner's "601 Photographs" show and Chase's Drums and Drones series follow.

years.h: A one-off reunion for a Mick Rock documentary
years.p: The trio plays Bowie and Lou Reed covers with Money Mark and TV on the Radio's Jaleel Bunton.

years.cap: Karen O at Ohana Festival, Dana Point
yt: There Is No Modern Romance (short film)
years.h: Fever to Tell comes back on vinyl, with a tour film
years.p: A deluxe reissue adds demos and unreleased songs. The short film There Is No Modern Romance shows the 2003 tour onstage and off, and the band plays its first shows in four years after Sound on Sound Fest is cancelled.
years.xp:
The band's note: "A friend of a friend kept asking if we were ever gonna put Fever to Tell out on vinyl as it hasn't been on vinyl in 10 years. That's not right."

Lizzy Goodman's oral history Meet Me in the Bathroom, out that year, tells the band's story alongside the Strokes and Interpol. The 2022 film of the book does too.

eras.title: Cool It Down, then quietly
eras.text: Signed to Secretly Canadian, they made an eight-song album about a burning planet with Sitek, and critics called it their most consistent. Then they took the old songs into theaters and played them softly.

years.h: Back on an independent: Secretly Canadian
years.p: The band signs to Secretly Canadian and announces new music and shows on social media.

yt: 'Spitting Off the Edge of the World' video
years.h: 'Spitting Off the Edge of the World', with Perfume Genius
years.p: The comeback single features [[Perfume Genius|c4ff10e0-ae5a-467d-a409-6e0b4bf241eb]], gets a Grammy nomination, and its video is directed by Cody Critcheloe, who drew the Fever to Tell cover nineteen years earlier.
years.xp: In 2025 the song turned up in the film The Gorge and topped two Billboard digital charts.

years.h: Cool It Down: eight songs, nine years after Mosquito
years.p: Recorded at Sonic Ranch in Texas, Federal Prism in California and Zinner's basement. A dollar from every pre-order goes to ClientEarth.
years.xp: Sitek co-produced with Justin Raisen and Andrew Wyatt. The album got the band's fourth nomination for Best Alternative Music Album.

years.h: The Hidden in Pieces tour plays the old songs softly
years.p: Theaters only, the catalog rearranged. At the Royal Albert Hall the Times' Mark Beaumont called it "one of the greatest Royal Albert Hall shows yet."

years.h: The Royal Albert Hall show becomes their first live album
years.p: Recordings from the London stop of Hidden in Pieces come out as a live album.
